questions.prompt: template <class T> T add(T a, T b); What happens with add(1, 2.5)?
options: T becomes double and the result is 3.5
The call compiles but is undefined behavior
Compile error: T is deduced as both int and double
T becomes int and the result is 3
questions.explanation: Each function parameter must deduce the same T; int and double conflict. Use add<double>(...) or two template parameters.

questions.prompt: Welford's algorithm processes {2, 4, 6}. What is the sample variance (divide by n-1)? Give a number with 2 decimals.
Which declaration can be used as the size of a std::array?
questions.explanation: An array size is a template argument and must be a constant expression; a run-time const is not.

questions.prompt: A constexpr table of int squares is built with make_squares<250>(). How many bytes does the array occupy (4-byte int)? Give an integer.
What does 'if constexpr' do in a template?
options: It evaluates the condition at run time but caches the result for later calls
It discards the untaken branch at compile time, so that branch need not be valid for T
It forces the condition to be true and ignores the else branch for every T
It makes the whole enclosing function constexpr and callable at compile time
questions.explanation: Discarded statements are not instantiated, which lets one template body handle types with different valid operations.

questions.prompt: A function template is declared in util.h and its body is only in util.cpp. main.cpp calls it with int. What do you most likely get?
options: A linker error: undefined reference to the int instantiation
A run-time exception thrown on the first call
It works, because the linker instantiates it on demand
A compile error inside util.cpp when it is built
questions.explanation: The compiler could not instantiate the template while compiling main.cpp because it did not see the body.

questions.prompt: Your generic mean(const Container&) is called with a std::vector<std::string> and prints a 40-line error. Show how to improve the diagnostic in C++17 and name the C++20 feature that improves it further.
rubric: Explains that the message states the unmet assumption in one line.
Names C++20 concepts / requires clauses, which report an unsatisfied constraint at the call site.
questions.explanation: Rubric-guided: compare your answer with each rubric point; this question is not automatically graded.
